q8.answer: The merge is a MERGE into dw.orders keyed on order_id, with the update branch guarded by WHEN MATCHED AND s.updated_at >= t.updated_at. An older copy never overwrites a newer one, and an identical re-applied row is a harmless no-op because of >= rather >.

q9.answer: It is stored in the warehouse, in the single row of etl.control (orders_nightly). It is set to GREATEST(hwm, cutoff), where cutoff is the replica's now() taken once at the start of the attempt. This happens inside the step 6 warehouse transaction, in the same commit as the MERGE, along with last_success_run_date.

q10.answer: The data merge and the hwm/last_success_run_date update commit in one warehouse transaction, and dashboards read committed state only. They see either the whole night or none of it. Staging is a separate table that dashboards do not read.

q11.answer: The failed attempt's staged data is discarded, because stg.orders_nightly is truncated at the start of every attempt and its warehouse transaction rolled back. The retry re-reads hwm from etl.control, which is unchanged, so it extracts the window starting at hwm minus 2 hours with a fresh cutoff. It never reuses the failed attempt's cutoff.

q12.answer: For each mismatched order-creation day it re-reads all of that day's rows from the replica, soft-deleted ones included, loads them into stg.orders_recon, and applies the same guarded MERGE in a warehouse transaction. It does not touch the nightly hwm.
